dispute_ticket.description: My receipt for Tuesday night shows S$27.90 with a S$3.00 ERP line, but I thought the ERP was already inside the fare. Can you check this? Also the driver sent me messages through the app the day after the trip, which I was not expecting.

chat_logs.content: Hi, I'm at the Raffles Place taxi stand.
Hi Mei Ling, Daniel from last night's ride. I kept your number from the trip. You left a really nice impression, would love to take you out for coffee or dinner sometime.
Not sure if you saw my message. No pressure, just say yes and I'll book a table for Saturday.
I'm not interested. Please stop messaging me.

app_events.details: ERP gantry crossed at Cross Street, S$3.00.
Trip completed; fare S$24.90 + ERP S$3.00 = S$27.90.

erp_pass_through.text: Governs ERP and toll charges. A true value means the actual ERP charge incurred on the trip is passed on to the rider and is shown on the receipt.

refund_at_ryde_discretion.text: Governs refunds on this trip. A true value means Ryde may refund beyond the strict rules where the facts justify it. It does not create a right to a refund.

expected_outcome.reason: The fare question alone would be dismissed: the receipt shows base S$24.90 plus ERP S$3.00 = S$27.90, and the 22:08:00 gantry event confirms the S$3.00 ERP was really incurred and passes through to the rider. But the chat shows the driver messaging the rider the next day: at 20:41:00 on 2026-10-21 he says he kept her number, asks her out for coffee or dinner, and at 08:15:00 on 2026-10-22 he presses again. She replies at 08:20:00 that she is not interested and asks him to stop. That is unwanted romantic contact by the driver after the trip, so Policy v2.1 s5.2 applies: a person decides. No automated verdict or refund.
